title: Google Evaluates Gemini 4 Carbon As It Seeks To Close AI Coding Gap
key_facts: Google is testing an internal version of Gemini 4, codenamed Carbon, according to a Business Insider report.
Carbon was recently made available on Google's internal coding platform, Jetski, and could be an updated version of Gemini 4 Argon.
An employee who tested Carbon told Business Insider its coding performance felt comparable to Anthropic's Opus 5.5, and said more testing is needed; another employee also praised the updated model.
Internal documents show Google has evaluated several Gemini 4 versions under the codenames Argon, Barium and Carbon; Barium-B was chosen for release as Argon.
Google has not confirmed whether Carbon will be released publicly or under a separate name.
Google plans to give Argon first to partners in its Fairwind Programme, which tests new models for cybersecurity vulnerabilities, before a wider rollout.
